decision.decision: Test capture and timeout handling from Sprint 189 (review follow-up requested in decision 1830 and next-step 1407; 1830 is not a standing waiver). Measured cause: the root 'core' vitest project runs the product-reality git-range and census specs in parallel with about 530 other files — the five slowest files in the root-core capture were archive-workflow.s188 (62 s), workflow.s188 (61 s), sprint-wide-movers.s185 (53 s), public-head-equivalence.s185 (48 s) and fresh-composition.s187 (40 s) — while packages/mcp-server's own project runs the same specs with fileParallelism:false and passed them; the timed-out test shells out to git diff four times over a growing sprint range under the global 20 s per-test budget and took 1.1 s in isolation. Both projects execute those specs, so every capture currently counts them twice. (a) Sprint 189 gives the git-range/census tests an explicit per-test timeout of 60 s (vitest's own advice for long-running tests) or moves them under a serial product-reality project, and removes the double execution so each spec is counted once per capture; this lands with the sprint branch and is captured there. (b) Retry policy: a wall-clock timeout with no assertion failure triggers exactly one isolated rerun of the affected file, retained beside the original; if it passes with unchanged bytes, the capture is accepted with the timeout disclosed as an observed timeout and no full-population recapture. An assertion failure, or a second timeout of the same test in isolation, requires a code fix and one corrective full capture. At most two full four-suite captures per sprint without a new decision. (c) The four-suite capture stays once per sprint at the closeout mission; no per-mission captures.

application: The initial capture has 15 actual AssertionErrors, so clause (b) requires code fixes and one corrective full capture. The memo's no-full-recapture timeout shorthand is read with its cited #1833 exception; no lone-timeout recapture or third full capture is used.
